label: Тебя
description: Object-form sentences that train how 'you' behaves after verbs and prepositions.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Object pronoun after a verb. 1. 'Тебя' is the object form of 'ты'. 2. 'Видит' is third-person singular and stays stable. 3. This sentence teaches how pronouns shift when they stop being the subject.
Strategic focus: Simple transitive verb. 1. 'Тебя' is the direct object. 2. 'Ждет' is third-person singular. 3. This is a common real-life sentence for timing and meeting.

Strategic focus: Plural subject plus object pronoun. 1. 'Они' forces the plural verb form. 2. 'Знают' stays plural while 'тебя' remains the object form. 3. The sentence is ideal for hearing the contrast between subject and object roles.

Strategic focus: Object pronoun with location. 1. 'Тебя' is the object being waited for. 2. 'Дома' adds an everyday location. 3. This line is useful because it combines verb government with a stable place word.
Strategic focus: Direct object in a family sentence. 1. 'Тебя' is the person being called. 2. 'Зовет' is a common high-frequency verb. 3. The sentence is natural and easy to remember.
Strategic focus: Object pronoun in a plural environment. 1. 'Тебя' remains the object form. 2. 'Ждут' is plural and matches 'друзья'. 3. 'У двери' adds a practical spatial phrase.
Strategic focus: Preposition plus object form. 1. 'Без' requires the object form. 2. 'Тебя' follows the preposition naturally. 3. 'Не начинайте' gives the line a real conversational feel.
Strategic focus: Relevance through preposition. 1. 'Для тебя' expresses purpose or relevance. 2. 'Это' introduces the topic. 3. 'Важно' closes the sentence with a concise evaluation.
Strategic focus: Motion toward the listener. 1. 'К тебе' uses a preposition that takes the object form. 2. 'Пришли' is plural past tense. 3. 'Гости' keeps the sentence vivid and practical.

Strategic focus: Prepositional phrase with object form. 1. 'С тобой' is the stable form used after 'с'. 2. 'Сидит' gives a clear spatial relation. 3. 'Учитель' is a concrete noun that makes the sentence easy to picture.

Strategic focus: Possession construction. 1. 'У тебя есть' is the standard Russian possession pattern. 2. 'Книга' is a simple feminine noun. 3. The sentence is useful because it contrasts possession with English-style subject ownership.

Strategic focus: Negation of possession. 1. 'У тебя нет' is the negative possession pattern. 2. 'Времени' shows the genitive form after negation. 3. This is one of the most practical everyday sentences in Russian.

Strategic focus: Preposition with object form. 1. 'После' requires the object/prepositional reference form. 2. 'Тебя' appears naturally after the preposition. 3. 'Сосед' is a common noun that keeps the sentence concrete.

Strategic focus: Fixed prepositional phrase. 1. 'Перед тобой' is the standard shape of the phrase. 2. 'Лежит' provides a stable visual action. 3. 'Письмо' is a compact object noun that works well with the scene.

Strategic focus: Object pronoun plus prepositional complement. 1. 'Тебя' is the person being asked. 2. 'Спрашивает' is a common interaction verb. 3. 'О книге' shows how a verb can add a second grammatical target after the object.
Strategic focus: Object pronoun with adverb. 1. 'Тебя' is the object being listened to. 2. 'Слушают' is plural and matches the subject. 3. 'Внимательно' makes the sentence feel alive and natural.

Strategic focus: Identity statement. 1. 'Тебя зовут' is a fixed naming construction. 2. The phrase does not use a subject pronoun the way English does. 3. This is a crucial survival phrase to internalize.

Strategic focus: Past absence. 1. 'Тебя не было' is a common Russian absence pattern. 2. 'Дома' keeps the location simple. 3. The sentence teaches that Russian can express absence without a direct English-style subject.

Strategic focus: Passive-like expectation. 1. 'Тебя' is the person who is waited for or expected. 2. 'Ждет' is singular and matches 'работа'. 3. This sentence is useful for seeing how roles can feel reversed from English.

Strategic focus: Preposition plus past event. 1. 'Без тебя' keeps the object form after the preposition. 2. 'Встреча началась' gives a natural event clause. 3. This is a very useful real-world sentence for explaining absence.
